openings.claim: Speculative: clearance-rich seating could restore the pointer more repeatably than visually tight fit, accommodating 18 mm replacement. Replace opposed tight-fit contacts with the same two adjacent plywood datum faces and an insertion stop per rod: end-stop contact, corner seating, hand tightening. Shared plywood cradle, bolt restraint, elastic seating bias and cord-retained hardware would make repeatability depend on seating order, not width.
openings.discriminator: Rival: tighter symmetric restraint improves stiffness and return. Datum seating predicts smaller post-exchange displacement despite clearance, including substitution; rival predicts tight-fit superiority. Improved return with increased loaded drift leaves repeatability/restraint dependencies unresolved. Two supplied trials suggest this discriminator, not proof.
openings.probe: Using six plywood pieces, eight bolts/nuts, four washers, two loops, 0.5 m cord and permitted tools, fabricate one captive cradle within 100 minutes; cut/drill only plywood. Compare datum-before-tightening versus opposed tightening with identical hardware; counterbalance order. Before timing, verify both pockets/retained hardware fit the 90 mm cube and loosened hardware stays attached. Within 20 testing minutes, each configuration gets twelve exchanges: five per original rod, then two 18 mm substitutions; four 10 N, ten-second load trials. Log stopwatch exchange time, target-card return, loaded displacement and retention. Stop on retention failure; stopped runs establish no performance success.
openings.uncertainty: Orientation unspecified: both pockets may not fit. Rigid datums and secure, unobstructive cord retention remain unproved. Hand assembly/adjustment only; no rod drilling, adhesive or permanent marks; preload must avoid permanent indentation. No component may fall free. Defeat: worse return than rival, escape from 2 mm target under load, exchange >=40 seconds, loose components, or exhausted fabrication/testing time. Insufficient measurement resolution/incomplete trials leave outcome unresolved. Enabling experiment, not deployment.

lineage.reason: Causal relation, rival, tests, caveats and uncertain fit retained.

decision: Retain one uncertain experiment. Success requires return within the 2 mm target circle and remaining there during loads. Seating discrimination is possible; stiffness, retention, orientation and test completion remain unproved.
